questions.question:
Study the given graph and answer the question that follows.

The graph shows the marks obtained by Riya and Rida in six subjects in the CBSE 12th exam. The maximum marks in Maths, Physics and Chemistry are 140, and that in English, IP and Biology are 180.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d47594fff2524a88d3e2eec9294f50fd9371d98aa87e053fe0ec9d4a18f00e3d.png] 

What is the difference between the percentage of marks obtained by Riya and Rida in IP?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marks obtained by Riya in IP = 150

Marks obtained by Rida in IP = 130

Maximum marks in IP = 180

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Marks obtained / Maximum marks) × 100

**Calculation:**

Difference in marks obtained by Riya and Rida = 150 - 130 = 20

So, % Difference = (20/180) × 100 = 1/9 × 100 = 11.11%

**∴ The difference between the percentage of marks obtained by Riya and Rida in IP is 11.11%.**

questions.question: A police travelling at 65 km/h is chasing a thief who is 1200 m away from him and is travelling at 41 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the policeman = 65 km/h

Speed of the thief = 41 km/h

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 1200 m

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = Speed of the policeman - Speed of the thief

Relative speed = 65 - 41

Relative speed = 24 km/h

Convert 1200 m to km:

1200 m = 1200 / 1000 km = 1.2 km

Time taken to catch the thief = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 1.2 km / 24 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 1.2 / 24

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.05 hours

Convert hours to minutes:

0.05 hours × 60 minutes/hour = 3 minutes

**The time taken by the policeman to catch the thief is 3 minutes.**

questions.question: The average age of Ruby and Soni is 40 years. The ratio of their ages is 11 : 5, respectively. What is the age (in years) of Soni?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average age of Ruby and Soni = 40 years.

The ratio of their ages (Ruby : Soni) = 11 : 5.

**Formula Used:**

Average age = (Sum of ages) / 2

**Calculation:**

Let the ages of Ruby and Soni be 11x and 5x, respectively.

Average age = (11x + 5x) / 2

40 = (11x + 5x) / 2

40 = 16x / 2

⇒ 40 = 8x

⇒ x = 40 / 8

⇒ x = 5

Age of Soni = 5x

⇒ Age of Soni = 5 × 5

⇒ Age of Soni = 25 years

**The age of Soni is 25 years.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells goods at 40% loss on cost price but uses 25% less weight. What is his percentage profit or loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The shopkeeper sells goods at a 40% loss on cost price.

The shopkeeper uses 25% less weight.

**Formula Used:**

Effective Profit or Loss Percentage = [(Loss% on Cost Price) / (1 - Fractional Reduction in Weight)]

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) at 40% loss = CP - 40% of CP

⇒ SP = 100 - 40

⇒ SP = 60 units

Actual weight used = 75% of the original weight

Fractional reduction in weight = 25% = 0.25

Effective Selling Price (considering 25% less weight) = SP / 0.75

⇒ Effective SP = 60 / 0.75

⇒ Effective SP = 80 units

Percentage Profit or Loss = [(Effective SP - CP) / CP] × 100

⇒ Percentage Profit or Loss = [(80 - 100) / 100] × 100

⇒ Percentage Profit or Loss = -20%

**The shopkeeper incurs a 20% loss.**

questions.question: The ratio of red to green sweets in a bag is 3 : 4. How many red sweets are there in the bag if the number of green sweets is 120?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of red to green sweets = 3:4

Number of green sweets = 120

**Formula Used:**

Number of red sweets = (Ratio of red sweets / Ratio of green sweets) × Number of green sweets

**Calculation:**

Number of red sweets = (3 / 4) × 120

⇒ Number of red sweets = 3 × (120 / 4)

⇒ Number of red sweets = 3 × 30

⇒ Number of red sweets = 90

**The number of red sweets in the bag is 90.**

questions.question: A laptop charger is sold for Rs. 2,540 in cash or for a down payment of Rs. 1,340 in cash together with Rs. 1,205 to be paid after one month. Find the rate of interest charged in the instalment scheme.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cash price of the laptop charger = Rs. 2,540

Down payment = Rs. 1,340

Amount to be paid after one month = Rs. 1,205

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest formula: SI = (P × R × T) / 100

Where:

 
• P = Principal amount (Rs. 1,200)
 
• R = Rate of interest per annum
 
• T = Time (1 month = 1/12 year)

**Calculation:**

Correct Principal amount P = 2,540 - 1,340 = 1,200

Interest amount I = 1,205 - 1,200 = 5

Using the Simple Interest formula:

5 = (1,200 × R × 1/12) / 100

⇒ 5 = (1,200 × R) / 1,200

⇒ R = 5%

**The rate of interest charged in the instalment scheme is 5% p.a.**

questions.solution:

PR = 40 cm

QR = 60 cm

Area of a triangle = 0.5 × base × height

Heron's formula for the area of a triangle: Area = √{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} 

where s = (a + b + c) / 2

**Calculation:**

a = 40 cm

b = 40 cm

c = 60 cm

s = (40 + 40 + 60) / 2

s = 70 cm

Using Heron's formula:

Area = √{70(70-40)(70-40)(70-60)} 

Area = √{70 × 30 × 30 × 10} 

Area = √{630000} 

Area = 300√ 7 cm²

Let h be the altitude from vertex Q to side PR.

Area = 0.5 × PR × h

300√ 7 = 0.5 × 40 × h

⇒ h = (300√ 7 × 2) / 40

⇒ h = (600√ 7) / 40

⇒ h = 15√ 7

**The altitude from the vertex Q to side PR is 15√ 7 cm.**

questions.question: Nirmal completed the school project in 45 days. How many days will Amit take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Nirmal?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Nirmal to complete the project = 45 days

Amit is 25% more efficient than Nirmal

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency and Time are inversely proportional.

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of Nirmal be 100 units.

Then, efficiency of Amit = 100 + 25 = 125 units

Since Efficiency ∝ 1/Time, we have:

Time taken by Amit = (Efficiency of Nirmal / Efficiency of Amit) × Time taken by Nirmal

⇒ Time taken by Amit = (100 / 125) × 45

⇒ Time taken by Amit = (4 / 5) × 45

⇒ Time taken by Amit = 36 days

**Amit will take 36 days to complete the same work.**

questions.question: Find the surface area (in cm²) of a cardboard box in the shape of a cuboid whose length is 60 cm. breadth is half its length and height is one-third of its breadth.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the cuboid (l) = 60 cm

Breadth of the cuboid (b) = ½ of its length = 60/2 = 30 cm

Height of the cuboid (h) = ⅓ of its breadth = 30/3 = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a cuboid = 2(l×b + b×h + h×l)

**Calculation:**

Surface Area = 2(l×b + b×h + h×l)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(60×30 + 30×10 + 10×60)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(1800 + 300 + 600)

⇒ Surface Area = 2(2700)

⇒ Surface Area = 5400 cm²

**The surface area of the cardboard box is 5400 cm².**
